title: Algebraic graded presentation of the tensor ideal sequences
statement: Let j:Z→X be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion], L an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and J=j.ker [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] with J²=0 [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Write η_d:L^d→j_*j^*L^d for the tensor-pullback adjunction unit in every nonnegative degree d [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. There exists a TensorGradedPresentation of these sequences: commutative O_X-algebra sheaves B,C and p:B→C [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf], an O_X-module K and inclusion i:K→B [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module], with 0→K→B→C→0 short exact and products of local sections in ker p equal to zero. It includes maps b_d:L^d→B, c_d:j_*j^*L^d→C, k_d:ker η_d→K, explicit quotient projections q_d=π_d,3, and morphisms π_d of short complexes from this extension to the degree-d kernel sequence. The maps k_d exhibit K as the sheaf coproduct of the degreewise kernels. The equations b_d;p=η_d;c_d and k_d;i=ker.ι;b_d hold. The diagonal composites c_d;π_d,3 and k_d;π_d,1 are identities, and k_a;π_d,1=0 for a≠d. On every open U, multiplication satisfies b_a(s)b_d(t)=b_(a+d)((tensorPowAddIso a d)^(-1)(s⊗t)). The statement asserts no cohomology boundary or action equation.

proof.text: Obtain the graded algebra quotient A, its canonical degree data D, and the square-zero kernel theorem. Construct the core explicitly with I=kernel(p), i=kernel.ι(p), and the fields of A and D. For the full presentation use A.b_multiply; the universal multiplication assertion for arbitrary cores is not used.
